logic.1V8: both supplied at 3.3 V; outputs are 3.3 V -> use the 3.3 V timer pad as planned

IR_RX (QTIMER1_TIMER1, capture) from the selected receiver
notes: Vishay TSOP parts are poorly stocked in SMD: TSOP75338 (as fitted in Kiisu V4b) 35-60 pieces per variant; TSOP75438WTT C7074088 2,464 at $2.22 (6.8 x 3.0 x 2.35 mm, 2.5-5.5 V) is the lower-profile stocked Vishay alternative; through-hole TSOP38238 C141632 has 75,471.

Learning: Vishay TSMP58000/TSMP77000/TSMP98000 have zero stock; TSMP95000TR (side-view taped) is the only stocked carrier-out part found. A bare photodiode option is Everlight PD15-22B/TR8 C161211 (16,525, 940 nm filtered) but it needs an amplifier/comparator and no circuit for that was read.

The IRM demodulates 38 kHz best; remotes at 36/40/56 kHz are received with reduced range (band-pass curve not transcribed). The TSMP95000 covers 30-60 kHz and returns the carrier itself, so the brain can measure the carrier frequency.
Window: both receivers and the LEDs are 940 nm; the TSMP/IRM packages are themselves IR filters.
pin_plan_conflicts: One IR_RX pin but two receivers proposed: add a 2:1 select (expander line) or a second capture pin.
No enable lines planned for the receivers' supply (about 0.75 mA always-on otherwise).
